node.title: Re: In Net::DNS::RR what is the 'can' method? (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
It's probably [doc://UNIVERSAL]::can.

Update: Yep, looks like it. [doc://UNIVERSAL] is Perl's implicit base class for all objects. can queries whether the object has that method (including via inheritance). It looks like the [mod://Net::DNS] docs are suggesting to use [wp://duck typing] here to tell whether the [mod://Net::DNS::RR] subclass has the address method. An alternative would be to use isa (also from [doc://UNIVERSAL]) to see if an object is of a certain class (or is one of its subclasses) and therefore supports that class's methods. The thing about that is though that you'd have to test against a whole list of [mod://Net::DNS::RR] subclasses. As long as all of the subclasses' address methods behave the same, duck typing is safe here, and easier.
